title: IL SB2909: SCH CD-TEACHER EVALUATION-AI

obligations: Each school district to which Article 24A applies shall establish a teacher evaluation plan that ensures each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once in the course of every 2 or 3 school years as provided in this Section (Sec. 24A-5, introductory paragraph)

Each school district shall establish a teacher evaluation plan that ensures each teacher not in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every school year and each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every 2 school years, except that any teacher rated needs improvement or unsatisfactory must be evaluated at least once in the school year following that rating (Sec. 24A-5, paragraphs (1) and (2))

No later than September 1, 2022, each school district must establish a plan ensuring each teacher in contractual continued service rated excellent or proficient is evaluated at least once in the course of the 3 school years after receipt of the rating and implement an informal teacher observation plan ensuring each such teacher is informally observed at least once in the course of the 2 school years after receipt of the rating (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph after paragraph (2))
The evaluation plan shall comply with the requirements of this Section and of any rules adopted by the State Board of Education (Sec. 24A-5)
The plan shall include a description of each teacher's duties and responsibilities and of the standards to which that teacher is expected to conform (Sec. 24A-5)
The plan shall include personal observation of the teacher in the classroom by the evaluator, unless the teacher has no classroom duties (subsection (a))
The plan shall include consideration of the teacher's attendance, planning, instructional methods, classroom management, where relevant, and competency in the subject matter taught (subsection (b))
The plan shall include rating of the performance of all teachers as excellent, proficient, needs improvement, or unsatisfactory (subsection (e))
The plan shall include specification as to the teacher's strengths and weaknesses, with supporting reasons for the comments made (subsection (f))
The plan shall include inclusion of a copy of the evaluation in the teacher's personnel file and provision of a copy to the teacher (subsection (g))

Within 30 school days after an evaluation rating a teacher in contractual continued service as needs improvement, the evaluator, in consultation with the teacher, shall develop a professional development plan directed to the areas that need improvement and any supports the district will provide (subsection (h))

Within 30 school days after an evaluation rating a teacher in contractual continued service as unsatisfactory, the district shall develop and commence a remediation plan designed to correct deficiencies cited, provided the deficiencies are deemed remediable; for unsatisfactory tenured teachers the remediation plan shall provide for 90 school days of remediation within the classroom unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides for a shorter duration; evaluations issued pursuant to this Section shall be issued within 10 days after the conclusion of the respective remediation plan (subsection (i))

The remediation plan shall include participation by the teacher rated unsatisfactory, an evaluator, and a consulting teacher selected by the evaluator who meets specified criteria; if no teachers who meet these criteria are available within the district, the district shall request and the applicable regional office of education shall supply an individual who meets these criteria (subsection (j))

The plan shall include a midpoint and final evaluation by an evaluator during and at the end of the remediation period; a written copy of the evaluations and ratings shall be provided to and discussed with the teacher within 10 school days after the date of the evaluation unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides to the contrary; the consulting teacher shall provide advice and participate in developing the remediation plan, but the final decision as to the evaluation shall be done solely by the evaluator unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides to the contrary (subsection (k))

The plan shall include reinstatement to the evaluation schedule for any teacher in contractual continued service who achieves a rating equal to or better than satisfactory or proficient in the school year following a rating of needs improvement or unsatisfactory (subsection (l))

The plan shall include dismissal in accordance with subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 24-16.5 or 34-85 of any teacher who fails to complete any applicable remediation plan with a rating equal to or better than a satisfactory or proficient rating; districts and teachers subject to dismissal hearings are precluded from compelling the testimony of consulting teachers at such hearings (subsection (m))

If a teacher in contractual continued service successfully completes a remediation plan following a rating of unsatisfactory and receives a subsequent rating of unsatisfactory in any overall performance evaluation within the 36 month period following completion, the school district may forgo remediation and seek dismissal in accordance with subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 34-85 (subsection (n))

Teachers who are due to be evaluated in the last year before they are set to retire shall be offered the opportunity to waive their evaluation and to retain their most recent rating, unless the teacher was last rated as needs improvement or unsatisfactory; the school district may still reserve the right to evaluate a teacher provided the district gives notice to the teacher at least 14 days before the evaluation and a reason for evaluating the teacher (subsection (o))

An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment; however, an artificial intelligence tool may be used to support the evaluator in administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)

A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance; however, an artificial intelligence tool may be used by a teacher to support the teacher in administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 shall determine how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)

If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool must be disclosed to the teacher being evaluated; if a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose must be disclosed to the evaluator evaluating the teacher (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)

If the Governor has declared a disaster due to a public health emergency pursuant to Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act that suspends in person instruction, the timelines in this Section connected to the commencement and completion of any remediation plan are waived; except if the parties mutually agree otherwise and the agreement is in writing, any remediation plan that had been in place for more than 45 days prior to the suspension of in person instruction shall resume when in person instruction resumes and any remediation plan that had been in place for fewer than 45 days prior to the suspension shall be discontinued and a new remediation period shall begin when in person instruction resumes (Sec. 24A-5, disaster paragraph)
prohibitions: An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating, such as excellent, proficient, need improvement, or unsatisfactory, for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)

A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)

Districts and teachers subject to dismissal hearings are precluded from compelling the testimony of consulting teachers at such hearings under subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 24-16.5 or 34-85, either as to the rating process or for opinions of performances by teachers under remediation (subsection (m))

Passed 2026-07-10. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

Amends the Illinois School Code teacher evaluation provisions. It requires school districts to establish teacher evaluation plans with specified frequency, components, and remediation procedures. It adds restrictions on artificial intelligence: evaluators cannot use AI to assign scores or ratings requiring professional judgment, teachers cannot use AI to generate evidence of professional practice, but AI may support administrative tasks, and any AI use must be disclosed.

Who it applies to

  • School districts to which Article 24A of the School Code applies (Sec. 24A-5)
  • Teachers in contractual continued service (Sec. 24A-5)
  • Teachers not in contractual continued service (Sec. 24A-5)
  • Evaluators (Sec. 24A-5)
  • The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 (Sec. 24A-5)

Effective date

8-15-25

Key definitions

  • Performance ratings: 'excellent', 'proficient', 'needs improvement', or 'unsatisfactory' (subsection (e))
  • Professional development plan: a plan directed to the areas that need improvement and any supports that the district will provide to address the areas identified as needing improvement (subsection (h))
  • Remediation plan: a plan designed to correct deficiencies cited, provided the deficiencies are deemed remediable, and for unsatisfactory tenured teachers shall provide for 90 school days of remediation within the classroom unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides for a shorter duration (subsection (i))
  • Consulting teacher: an educational employee as defined in the Illinois Educational Labor Relations Act, has at least 5 years' teaching experience, and a reasonable familiarity with the assignment of the teacher being evaluated, and who received an 'excellent' rating on his or her most recent evaluation (subsection (j))
  • Artificial intelligence tool: not defined in the text (Sec. 24A-5)

Obligations

  • Each school district to which Article 24A applies shall establish a teacher evaluation plan that ensures each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once in the course of every 2 or 3 school years as provided in this Section (Sec. 24A-5, introductory paragraph)
  • Each school district shall establish a teacher evaluation plan that ensures each teacher not in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every school year and each teacher in contractual continued service is evaluated at least once every 2 school years, except that any teacher rated needs improvement or unsatisfactory must be evaluated at least once in the school year following that rating (Sec. 24A-5, paragraphs (1) and (2))
  • No later than September 1, 2022, each school district must establish a plan ensuring each teacher in contractual continued service rated excellent or proficient is evaluated at least once in the course of the 3 school years after receipt of the rating and implement an informal teacher observation plan ensuring each such teacher is informally observed at least once in the course of the 2 school years after receipt of the rating (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph after paragraph (2))
  • The evaluation plan shall comply with the requirements of this Section and of any rules adopted by the State Board of Education (Sec. 24A-5)
  • The plan shall include a description of each teacher's duties and responsibilities and of the standards to which that teacher is expected to conform (Sec. 24A-5)
  • The plan shall include personal observation of the teacher in the classroom by the evaluator, unless the teacher has no classroom duties (subsection (a))
  • The plan shall include consideration of the teacher's attendance, planning, instructional methods, classroom management, where relevant, and competency in the subject matter taught (subsection (b))
  • The plan shall include rating of the performance of all teachers as excellent, proficient, needs improvement, or unsatisfactory (subsection (e))
  • The plan shall include specification as to the teacher's strengths and weaknesses, with supporting reasons for the comments made (subsection (f))
  • The plan shall include inclusion of a copy of the evaluation in the teacher's personnel file and provision of a copy to the teacher (subsection (g))
  • Within 30 school days after an evaluation rating a teacher in contractual continued service as needs improvement, the evaluator, in consultation with the teacher, shall develop a professional development plan directed to the areas that need improvement and any supports the district will provide (subsection (h))
  • Within 30 school days after an evaluation rating a teacher in contractual continued service as unsatisfactory, the district shall develop and commence a remediation plan designed to correct deficiencies cited, provided the deficiencies are deemed remediable; for unsatisfactory tenured teachers the remediation plan shall provide for 90 school days of remediation within the classroom unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides for a shorter duration; evaluations issued pursuant to this Section shall be issued within 10 days after the conclusion of the respective remediation plan (subsection (i))
  • The remediation plan shall include participation by the teacher rated unsatisfactory, an evaluator, and a consulting teacher selected by the evaluator who meets specified criteria; if no teachers who meet these criteria are available within the district, the district shall request and the applicable regional office of education shall supply an individual who meets these criteria (subsection (j))
  • The plan shall include a midpoint and final evaluation by an evaluator during and at the end of the remediation period; a written copy of the evaluations and ratings shall be provided to and discussed with the teacher within 10 school days after the date of the evaluation unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides to the contrary; the consulting teacher shall provide advice and participate in developing the remediation plan, but the final decision as to the evaluation shall be done solely by the evaluator unless an applicable collective bargaining agreement provides to the contrary (subsection (k))
  • The plan shall include reinstatement to the evaluation schedule for any teacher in contractual continued service who achieves a rating equal to or better than satisfactory or proficient in the school year following a rating of needs improvement or unsatisfactory (subsection (l))
  • The plan shall include dismissal in accordance with subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 24-16.5 or 34-85 of any teacher who fails to complete any applicable remediation plan with a rating equal to or better than a satisfactory or proficient rating; districts and teachers subject to dismissal hearings are precluded from compelling the testimony of consulting teachers at such hearings (subsection (m))
  • If a teacher in contractual continued service successfully completes a remediation plan following a rating of unsatisfactory and receives a subsequent rating of unsatisfactory in any overall performance evaluation within the 36 month period following completion, the school district may forgo remediation and seek dismissal in accordance with subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 34-85 (subsection (n))
  • Teachers who are due to be evaluated in the last year before they are set to retire shall be offered the opportunity to waive their evaluation and to retain their most recent rating, unless the teacher was last rated as needs improvement or unsatisfactory; the school district may still reserve the right to evaluate a teacher provided the district gives notice to the teacher at least 14 days before the evaluation and a reason for evaluating the teacher (subsection (o))
  • An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment; however, an artificial intelligence tool may be used to support the evaluator in administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance; however, an artificial intelligence tool may be used by a teacher to support the teacher in administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 shall determine how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose of the artificial intelligence tool must be disclosed to the teacher being evaluated; if a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose must be disclosed to the evaluator evaluating the teacher (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • If the Governor has declared a disaster due to a public health emergency pursuant to Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act that suspends in person instruction, the timelines in this Section connected to the commencement and completion of any remediation plan are waived; except if the parties mutually agree otherwise and the agreement is in writing, any remediation plan that had been in place for more than 45 days prior to the suspension of in person instruction shall resume when in person instruction resumes and any remediation plan that had been in place for fewer than 45 days prior to the suspension shall be discontinued and a new remediation period shall begin when in person instruction resumes (Sec. 24A-5, disaster paragraph)

Prohibitions

  • An evaluator is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating, such as excellent, proficient, need improvement, or unsatisfactory, for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • A teacher is prohibited from using an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • Districts and teachers subject to dismissal hearings are precluded from compelling the testimony of consulting teachers at such hearings under subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 24-16.5 or 34-85, either as to the rating process or for opinions of performances by teachers under remediation (subsection (m))

Penalties and enforcement

The statute does not state specific penalties for violations of the artificial intelligence provisions. Enforcement of evaluation and remediation requirements is through existing teacher evaluation and dismissal procedures: a teacher who fails to complete a remediation plan with a rating equal to or better than satisfactory or proficient may be dismissed in accordance with subsection (d) of Section 24-12 or Section 24-16.5 or 34-85 (subsection (m)). The State Board of Education may adopt rules pursuant to this Section (Sec. 24A-5). No private right of action is stated in the text.

How it affects AI deployment

  • An evaluator cannot use an artificial intelligence tool to assign a numerical score or qualitative rating for any component of a teacher's evaluation or any evaluation task that requires professional judgment; AI may only support administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • A teacher cannot use an artificial intelligence tool to generate evidence of professional practice that will be used by an evaluator to evaluate the teacher's performance; AI may only support administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • The joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 determines how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o), so an organisation deploying AI in teacher evaluation must follow that committee's determinations (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose must be disclosed to the teacher being evaluated; if a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, the name and specific purpose must be disclosed to the evaluator (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • School districts must ensure their evaluation plans and practices do not allow AI to perform professional judgment tasks, and any AI use is limited to administrative support and disclosed (Sec. 24A-5)

Notable exemptions

  • This Section does not apply to teachers assigned to schools identified in an agreement entered into between the board of a school district operating under Article 34 and the exclusive representative of the district's teachers in accordance with Section 34-85c (Sec. 24A-5, introductory paragraph)
  • Teachers due to be evaluated in the last year before retirement may waive their evaluation and retain their most recent rating unless last rated needs improvement or unsatisfactory; the district may still evaluate with 14 days notice and a reason (subsection (o))
  • If the Governor has declared a disaster due to a public health emergency pursuant to Section 7 of the Illinois Emergency Management Agency Act that suspends in person instruction, the timelines connected to commencement and completion of any remediation plan are waived (Sec. 24A-5, disaster paragraph)
  • Nothing in this Section or Section 24A-4 shall be construed as preventing immediate dismissal of a teacher for deficiencies which are deemed irremediable or for actions which are injurious to or endanger the health or person of students in the classroom or school, or preventing the dismissal or nonrenewal of teachers not in contractual continued service for any reason not prohibited by applicable employment, labor, and civil rights laws (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph after AI paragraph)
  • Failure to strictly comply with the time requirements contained in Section 24A-5 shall not invalidate the results of the remediation plan (Sec. 24A-5, paragraph after AI paragraph)
  • In a district having a population of less than 500,000 with an exclusive bargaining agent, the bargaining agent may supply a roster of qualified teachers from whom the consulting teacher is to be selected (subsection (j))
  • An applicable collective bargaining agreement may provide for a shorter duration for the remediation plan for unsatisfactory tenured teachers (subsection (i))
  • An applicable collective bargaining agreement may provide to the contrary regarding the written copy discussion timeline and the final decision being solely by the evaluator (subsection (k))

Compliance steps

  • Establish a teacher evaluation plan that complies with Section 24A-5 and State Board of Education rules, including required frequency and components (Sec. 24A-5)
  • Ensure evaluators do not use artificial intelligence tools to assign numerical scores or qualitative ratings for any component requiring professional judgment; allow AI only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • Ensure teachers do not use artificial intelligence tools to generate evidence of professional practice used for evaluation; allow AI only for administrative tasks (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • Have the joint committee under subsection (b-5) of Section 24A-4 determine how artificial intelligence tools may be used in accordance with paragraphs (a) through (o) (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • If an evaluator uses an artificial intelligence tool, disclose its name and specific purpose to the teacher being evaluated; if a teacher uses an artificial intelligence tool, disclose its name and specific purpose to the evaluator (Sec. 24A-5, AI paragraph)
  • Implement all evaluation plan components: personal observation, consideration of attendance and instruction, ratings, strengths and weaknesses, personnel file copy, professional development plan for needs improvement within 30 days, remediation plan for unsatisfactory within 30 days with consulting teacher, midpoint and final evaluations, reinstatement, dismissal for failure, and retirement waiver (subsections (a) through (o))
  • Comply with disaster waiver timelines if the Governor declares a public health emergency that suspends in person instruction (Sec. 24A-5, disaster paragraph)
